what_its_for: Electrolyte-A Solution is used to replace fluids and minerals (like sodium, potassium, and chloride) that your body loses when you have diarrhea, vomiting, or heavy sweating. It helps prevent or treat dehydration, which means your body does not have enough water and salts to work properly.
how_to_take: Drink this solution slowly in small sips. Do not gulp large amounts at once, especially if you feel nauseated or have been vomiting. You can drink it at room temperature or chilled — whichever is more comfortable for you. Do not mix it with other liquids like juice or sports drinks unless your doctor or pharmacist says it is okay. Use the measuring cup or syringe that comes in the package to make sure you get the right amount.
dosing: The right amount depends on your age, weight, and how dehydrated you are. A common starting guide is: Adults and children over 10 years old: 1 to 2 liters (about 4 to 8 cups) over the first 4 hours, then continue sipping as needed. Children 1 to 10 years old: about 50 to 100 mL per kg of body weight over 4 hours. Infants under 1 year: follow your doctor's instructions carefully. Always follow the dose your doctor or pharmacist recommends for your specific situation.
missed_dose: Electrolyte-A Solution is not a medication you take on a strict schedule. If you forget to drink your usual amount, drink some as soon as you remember. Try to keep up with small, frequent sips throughout the day. The most important thing is to keep drinking enough to stay hydrated.
storage: Store unopened bottles at room temperature, away from heat and direct sunlight. Once you open the bottle, keep it in the refrigerator and use it within 48 hours. Do not freeze. Keep out of reach of children. Throw away any leftover solution after 48 hours of opening or by the expiration date on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking large amounts of plain water, sugary drinks like juice or soda, or sports drinks in place of this solution, as they do not have the right balance of salts and sugars for rehydration. Avoid alcohol and caffeine while you are dehydrated, as they can make dehydration worse. Do not add extra salt, sugar, or flavorings to the solution unless your doctor tells you to.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you or your child: cannot keep any fluids down after trying for 30 to 60 minutes; has signs of severe dehydration such as no urination for 8 or more hours, very dry mouth and lips, sunken eyes, extreme tiredness, or no tears when crying; has bloody or very dark diarrhea; has a high fever (over 102°F or 39°C in adults, or any fever in infants under 3 months); shows signs of confusion or unusual drowsiness; or if symptoms do not improve after 24 to 48 hours of using this solution.
when_it_works: You should start to feel better within a few hours of drinking the solution regularly. Signs that it is working include feeling less dizzy or lightheaded, urinating more normally, having a moist mouth, and having more energy. It may take 1 to 2 days for diarrhea or vomiting to fully improve.
special_populations: Infants and young children: Always talk to your pediatrician before giving this to a baby under 1 year old. Do not substitute this for breast milk or formula. Older adults: Elderly people are at higher risk for dehydration and may need more careful monitoring. Kidney disease patients: Talk to your doctor before using, as the extra potassium and sodium may not be safe for everyone with kidney problems. Pregnant or breastfeeding women: This solution is generally considered safe, but check with your doctor if you have concerns. Diabetics: Some formulations contain sugar; check the label or ask your pharmacist if you need a sugar-free option.
